fieldNotes.operationalStatus: OPERATIONAL. This blank-flag entry is the active Ozarka (BlueTriton / Primo Brands) bottling plant + distribution center at 9351 E Point Dr, Houston TX 77054 (the city's southwest industrial belt near the Medical Center, marketed by Nestle/BlueTriton as the 'South Houston' bottling facility, paired with the Pasadena plant). No closure news found. Macrae's Blue Book classifies the site as a manufacturer that 'manufactures bottled water'; directories also list it as a bottling water delivery/distribution center (~110 staff). 2022-11 Street View shows tall vertical process/storage SILOS behind the building, a fenced controlled gate with Ozarka-branded signage, multiple tractors and XTRA-lease trailers staged inside, and an active dock face. Satellite (2026 Maxar) shows trailers at the docks, a full trailer drop row along the rail, and pallets of finished product staged in the yard. Verdict: fully operational bottling plant.
fieldNotes.siteResolution: Given approximate coords (29.6650, -95.3850) landed ~2km east at a freeway interchange (solar field + residential), not an industrial site. Resolved the real plant via web search to 9351 E Point Dr, Houston TX 77054 (~29.6688, -95.4048), confirmed by satellite (large fenced industrial building with silos, dock face, trailer yard) and Street View (Ozarka gate signage, branded fence sign).
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE. 2022-11 Street View from E Point Dr (pano tW75nXdg5UqvujlvB_OOqA, headings 120-135) shows a chain-link-fenced perimeter with a sliding gate across the truck drive on the north side, with Ozarka-branded sign panels at the gate. Trucks/trailers are staged inside the fence line.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE. No staffed booth (1-3 vehicle footprint, multi-side windows) at the entrance. The gate signage instead reads as call-box / check-in instructions ('Visitor Entrance / Live call box for entry / ...Gate 3'-style wording), i.e. unmanned remote check-in.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: TRUE. There is a controlled truck gate but no guard shack; entry is by call box / intercom per the gate signage.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: South face of the main building carries a long continuous dock apron with a regular bay rhythm; counted ~20-24 dock positions across the south face in z20 imagery, plus the attached east hall has a few more. Honest estimate ~24, banded 10-25 conservatively (sits near the 25 boundary). Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Dedicated trailer drop row along the rail at the south edge: ~15-18 trailers parked perpendicular without tractors. Banded 10-25.
fieldNotes.dropYard: TRUE - the south rail-side row is a distinct trailer-storage strip separate from the active dock staging.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved internal yard between the gate, the silos, and the dock face acts as an inside-the-gate queue/staging area.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Short approach: the gate sits close to the building's north yard; the gate-to-dock internal path is modest. The deeper queuing happens in the internal yard (postGateStaging), not a long single-file approach lane.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: FALSE. E Point Dr is a low-traffic dead-end-style industrial street with ample paved apron at the gate; a short truck queue would not spill onto a public artery.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single fenced truck gate on the north (E Point Dr) serves both in and out. entryLanes/exitLanes estimated 1/1 from the single drive width; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Marked FALSE - docks read as one contiguous south-face bank; could not confirm a physically separate second ship/receive cluster. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban - dense Houston inner-loop industrial fabric (77054, near the Medical Center / SW Houston), surrounded by warehouses and rail, inside a major metro.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: FALSE - dense urban metro, strong cellular coverage expected.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE - a multi-track rail line runs immediately along the south property edge, but no spur enters the property; trailers, not rail cars, are loaded. The rail is adjacency only.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Two counted: the main bottling/warehouse building (with NW silos) plus its attached east production hall read as one complex with a large adjacent warehouse; a separate light-roof warehouse to the west and the small blue-roof structure to the NE appear to be different parcels/tenants and were excluded from the perimeter. Counted 2 within the Ozarka complex; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~14 acres of fenced building + yard footprint derived from the perimeter polygon (main complex only, excluding neighboring parcels).
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~8-10 at the south docks + ~15-18 in the rail-side drop row + a few in the internal yard = ~26 across the captured imagery; mixed-vintage tiles, approximate.
fieldNotes.scale: FALSE - no truck scale/weigh pad visible in the truck path.
